symptom: An interrupting boundary path written from MDL that runs to its last activity (`boundary event interrupting timer … { call microflow M.X; }`) was stored ending in EndOfBoundaryEventPathActivity — the terminator Studio Pro writes for a NON-interrupting path. An evaluator opening the result in Studio Pro reported mxcli 'mixing end of boundary path with End', and agents were unsure how either kind should end. Over MCP the same MDL was refused, since Studio Pro's interrupting constructor requires an End or a jump
cause: workflows.EndBoundaryEventPath, added to clear CE0105 (interrupting) and a runtime start failure (non-interrupting), appended the marker to every unended path whatever its kind, at all three call sites (CREATE's buildBoundaryEvents, the file mutator's and MCP's ALTER insert)
insight: **Measure the runtime before calling a stored shape a defect.** The obvious fear was that an interrupting path ending in the marker leaves an instance with no active path after the parent is aborted; on the 11.13.0 runtime (run --local, hsqldb, a 20-second timer, a marker after the task to show whether the main flow continued) the marker and an End behaved identically: instance Completed, EndTime set, the activity after the task never ran. That turned a would-be semantics fix into a shape fix and set its limits: change only where an End can stand (not under a parallel split or a non-interrupting path, CE1844 at any depth — already measured in PROPOSAL_workflow_end_activity), keep the marker elsewhere because it builds, and never invent a jump target. Probe trap worth skipping: an after-startup microflow that starts workflows runs before any user exists, so every XPath-targeted task fails 'User targeting returned no users' and no timer is ever armed — create and commit a user (with a password, or startup fails on validation) first. JDK 21 runs 11.13 but not 11.14+ (needs 25)
fix: A post-build pass replaces the trailing marker of each interrupting path with an End where endAllowed (main flow, outcomes, interrupting paths, event sub-process bodies; not parallel split paths or non-interrupting paths). ALTER computes endAllowed from the stored placement of the target (resolveStoredPlacement) and appends the End before the mutator, whose EndBoundaryEventPath then leaves an ended path alone. describe now prints `end workflow;` there and the describe → exec round trip is Unchanged
